subject: Prototype addendum: hybrid top-up vs milestone voucher pathway — recommendation and approvals
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@cardinalai.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prototype addendum: hybrid top-up vs milestone voucher pathway — initial proposal

Hi Elena,

Great to talk this morning — thanks for walking me through Cardinal's evaluation goals for the prototype. Per our discussion, I've attached a short addendum draft that shows two bridging options to keep the prototype running through your scale tests while we finalize a Dedicated capacity quote.

Option A — Hybrid top-up (recommended):
- Pay-as-you-go top-up bucket applied to the existing trial; flexible burst capacity; monthly reconciliation.
- 15% one-time discount applied to the top-up bucket if Cardinal converts to a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days of prototype end.

Option B — Milestone vouchers:
- A set of three vouchers tied to product milestones (ingestion performance, 90% pass rate on throughput, end-to-end latency under 300ms).
- Vouchers redeemable against usage; no upfront commit required.

My recommendation is Option A — it preserves momentum, reduces procurement friction, and gives a clear incentive for conversion. That said, I know Procurement will have preferences for invoiceable milestones.

Next steps: if Procurement is okay with the hybrid approach we can send a short addendum + DocuSign and provision the burst bucket within 24 hours. If they prefer vouchers, I can surface a slightly smaller discount but make all three vouchers convertible into committed credits.

I've attached the draft addendum and a one-page Q1 usage snapshot from your sandbox so you can see likely burn. Happy to call through with Procurement.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Connor — useful framing. A few quick questions from our side before we loop Procurement formally:

1) For Option A, is the 15% discount off list for all token consumption in the top-up bucket or only for model-run tokens (inference) excluding embeddings?
2) How does the reconciliation work if we overshoot the monthly bucket? Is there an overage rate or roll-forward?
3) For Option B, we like the predictability but worried vouchers will slow review. Can vouchers be partially redeemed (e.g., 40% on milestone 1, 60% on milestone 2)?

Procurement: tagging you on this thread for visibility — we prefer a single invoice line item if possible.

Subject: Re: Prototype addendum: hybrid top-up vs milestone voucher pathway — clarifications

Elena — quick answers inline:  
1) Discount scope: the 15% in Option A applies to all usage consumed from the top-up bucket (generation and embeddings). If you want embeddings excluded we can price-adjust (would reduce the discount to ~10%).
2) Reconciliation: monthly roll-forward up to one billing cycle; if you exceed the roll-forward the overage is charged at a 20% discounted overage rate relative to list. We can also cap overage — e.g., stop provisioning after X tokens and notify your team.
3) Vouchers: yes — they can be split across milestones. The trade-off is administrative overhead (Procurement tends to prefer simpler invoices).

If Procurement wants single-line invoicing, Option A maps cleanly to that. I'll draft a single-line addendum version for Procurement review.

Connor
